1. SUPPORTED - Mei’s Context Engineering survey notes that many surveys focus on specialized subfields, motivating a unified taxonomy.
2. CONTRADICTED - Mei’s survey states that PoSE extends context to 128K tokens, not 256K.
3. SUPPORTED - Mei defines context engineering as dynamically retrieving, selecting, formatting, and assembling contextual components.
4. SUPPORTED - Liu et al.’s Lost in the Middle shows substantial performance changes based on the position of relevant information.
5. SUPPORTED - MemGPT distinguishes main context, available during inference, from external context stored outside the fixed context window.
6. SUPPORTED - Zhang et al.’s ACE identifies context collapse as a failure mode of repeatedly rewriting accumulated context.
7. NOT FOUND - The documents do not establish that DSPy itself regularly defeats strong reference models across both agentic and specialized tasks.
8. SUPPORTED - Hsieh et al.’s RULER includes retrieval, multi-hop tracing, aggregation, and question-answering tasks using controllable synthetic contexts.
9. CONTRADICTED - RULER evaluates 17 models across 13 representative task configurations, not eight assessment scenarios.
10. SUPPORTED - Wu et al.’s LongMemEval reports approximately a 30% accuracy drop for commercial assistants and long-context models on sustained-interaction memory.
11. NOT FOUND - The documents do not report substantially higher retention from assistants that proactively prompt users about private history.
12. CONTRADICTED - Yao et al.’s ReAct reports improvements over imitation and reinforcement-learning methods on ALFWorld and WebShop.
13. SUPPORTED - Lewis et al.’s RAG paper describes Jeopardy generation as requiring precise, factual, and specific clues about target entities.
14. SUPPORTED - Park et al.’s Generative Agents architecture combines recency, importance, and relevance to retrieve memories for the current situation.
15. CONTRADICTED - Hsieh et al.’s RULER discussion reports BABILong’s counting task at 28% even at 0K context, not only with extensive distractors.
16. NOT FOUND - Mem0 proposes its own graph-enhanced variant in the same paper; the documents do not identify a separate paper making that proposal.
17. CONTRADICTED - Brown et al.’s GPT-3 paper, not a BERT paper, reports prompting without parameter updates and evaluates language, reasoning, and mathematical tasks.
18. CONTRADICTED - Brown et al. discuss scaling performance with model size and compute; the relationship is not attributed entirely to learning-rate and batch-size optimization.
19. SUPPORTED - The Gemini 1.5 report states that Flash achieves nearly perfect retrieval across text, video, and audio up to approximately 2M tokens.
20. SUPPORTED - The Gemini 1.5 report describes over 99% retrieval up to 10M tokens and characterizes this as a major advance over Claude 3 and GPT-4 Turbo context capabilities.
